questions.text: "I stopped smoking." — What happened?
opts: I stopped in order to smoke
questions.correct: The habit of smoking ended
questions.hint: "Stop + gerund" = the activity ENDS. She no longer smokes. ✅

questions.text: "Try + gerund" suggests:
opts: Effort toward a goal that may fail
Experiment — test this and see what happens
questions.correct: Experiment — test this and see what happens
questions.hint: "Try + gerund = experiment/test." Close in meaning to "try out." ✅

questions.text: "I remember to call him." — What does this mean?
opts: I have a memory of calling him
I don't forget to call him (future task)
questions.correct: I don't forget to call him (future task)
questions.hint: "Remember + infinitive" = future task/obligation you keep in mind. ✅

questions.text: "She went on to become a professor." — This means:
opts: She moved to a new stage — became a professor after this point
She tried to become a professor
questions.correct: She moved to a new stage — became a professor after this point
questions.hint: "Go on + infinitive" = progression to a new stage. ✅

questions.text: Dr. Seitkali says "try + gerund" is close to what phrasal verb?
questions.correct: Try out
questions.hint: "Try + gerund is close in meaning to 'try out' — experiment, test it, see what happens." ✅

questions.text: "We regret to inform you that..." — "to inform" because:
opts: Formal announcement of bad news that follows
questions.correct: Formal announcement of bad news that follows
questions.hint: "Regret + infinitive" = formal introduction of bad news. Used in letters/announcements. ✅

questions.text: What is Kamila's main dilemma?
opts: Whether to go to Vienna for a semester or stay to finish her thesis on time
questions.correct: Whether to go to Vienna for a semester or stay to finish her thesis on time
questions.hint: "Whether to go for a semester or to stay here and finish my thesis on time." ✅

questions.text: What does Rustam suggest to reframe the decision?
opts: Stop seeing the options as opposed — imagine doing both
questions.correct: Stop seeing the options as opposed — imagine doing both
questions.hint: "Stop seeing them as a choice and start imagining how to do both." ✅

questions.text: What does Kamila regret?
opts: Not having raised the idea with her supervisor earlier
questions.correct: Not having raised the idea with her supervisor earlier
questions.hint: "I regret not having raised this with her earlier." ✅

questions.text: In the lecture, what test does Dr. Seitkali offer for "try + gerund"?
questions.correct: Think "try out"
questions.hint: Try + gerund is close in meaning to "try out" — use it as a test for the gerund meaning. ✅

questions.text: "Remember + gerund" is about:
questions.correct: A past memory
questions.hint: "Remember + gerund is about the past." = a memory of something that has already happened. ✅

questions.text: What does Dr. Seitkali explain about "stop + infinitive"?
opts: It expresses the purpose of stopping — why you stopped
It's the same as stop + gerund
questions.correct: It expresses the purpose of stopping — why you stopped
questions.hint: "Stop + infinitive expresses purpose — why you stopped." ✅

questions.text: "I tried to open the jar but it was sealed." — "tried + infinitive" means:
opts: I made an effort to open it (possibly failed)
questions.correct: I made an effort to open it (possibly failed)
questions.hint: "Try + infinitive" = effort toward a goal; the jar being sealed implies failure. ✅

questions.text: "She forgot meeting him." — This means:
opts: She was supposed to meet him but didn't show up
She met him but has no memory of it now
questions.correct: She met him but has no memory of it now
questions.hint: "Forget + gerund" = past event with no memory. She did meet him; she just forgot that it happened. ✅

questions.text: "In addition to examining X, the study also considers Y." — "examining" because:
questions.correct: "In addition to" = preposition → gerund
questions.hint: "In addition TO" — "to" = PREPOSITION → must use GERUND. ✅

questions.text: "It is essential to acknowledge the limitations." — "to acknowledge" because:
opts: "It + adj + to-infinitive" structure always uses infinitive
questions.correct: "It + adj + to-infinitive" structure always uses infinitive
questions.hint: "It is essential TO ACKNOWLEDGE." — "It + adj + to-inf" ALWAYS uses infinitive. ✅

questions.text: "The report needs ___." (gerund form, informal = needs to be updated)
questions.correct: updating
questions.hint: "The report needs UPDATING." = informal "needs + gerund" = formal "needs to be updated." ✅

questions.text: "She was happy to have been selected." — "to have been selected" is:
questions.correct: Passive perfect infinitive
questions.hint: "to have been selected" = passive perfect infinitive after adjective. ✅

questions.text: "Look forward to seeing you." — "seeing" (not "see") because:
questions.correct: "To" here is a preposition → gerund
questions.hint: "Look forward TO" — "to" = PREPOSITION → GERUND. NOT infinitive. ✅

questions.text: "Having finished the report, she felt relieved." — "Having finished" is:
questions.correct: Perfect gerund
questions.hint: "Having finished" = PERFECT GERUND (having + pp). Completed action before the result. ✅

questions.text: "She felt deep remorse." "Remorse" means:
opts: Deep guilt and regret about a past action
questions.correct: Deep guilt and regret about a past action
questions.hint: "remorse" = strong feeling of regret and guilt about something wrong you did.

questions.text: "It would be premature to conclude." "Premature" means:
opts: Too early; before there is sufficient evidence
questions.correct: Too early; before there is sufficient evidence
questions.hint: "premature" = happening too soon; before the right time.

questions.text: "The gerund after a preposition is obligatory." "Obligatory" means:
questions.correct: Required; must be used
questions.hint: "obligatory" = required by rule; you must do it.

questions.text: "The more idiomatic option." "Idiomatic" means:
opts: Natural to native speakers; typical of the language
questions.correct: Natural to native speakers; typical of the language
questions.hint: "idiomatic" = sounding natural; characteristic of how native speakers actually use the language.

questions.text: "I remember the activity persisting." "Persist" means:
questions.correct: Continue; not cease
questions.hint: "persist" = to continue; to remain unchanged; to not give up or stop.
